subject: Post-call: Integration & inference goals — Catalyst AI
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@catalyst.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@catalyst.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Integration & inference goals — Catalyst AI

Thanks again for a productive conversation earlier, Sara/Tom — appreciate the context and the demo of your current reranking flow. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page.

Recap of pain points you shared:
- P1: High tail latency when reranking with long context (search + convo history) causing UX drop-offs and rate-limit retries.
- P2: Quality drift in rerank ordering on new content types (multimodal snippets, code blocks).
- P3: Significant token cost at scale using synchronous full-context generation for follow-up responses.
- P4: Compliance constraint: must run in customer-managed Azure VNET with strict egress policies.

Primary goals discussed:
- Reduce rerank latency P95 to <120ms for top-10 candidates; ideal target <80ms for hot paths.
- Add streaming generation + partial ranking so UI can show progressive results for long responses.
- Introduce structured outputs (strict JSON schema) for downstream processors to avoid brittle parsing.
- Pilot embedding-based reranking to improve top-1 accuracy by ~6-10% while cutting per-query cost.

Integration asks / constraints we should cover:
- SDK: need a lightweight JS/Go client that supports streaming + function-calling hooks and an easy path to switch model variants.
- Function calling: ability to declare typed function signatures so your backend can safely execute actions from model output.
- Structured outputs: support enforceable output schemas and validation failures reported in the response metadata.
- Embeddings: must support 512 and 1536 dimensional embeddings (you currently have 1536 vectors) and a batch embed endpoint with latency SLOs.
- Private deployment: Redwood Private (VNET) option needed; confirm KMS/HSM integration and audit log export cadence.

Proposed next steps (owners & rough timing):
1) Redwood to produce a 1-page technical compatibility checklist and an integration playbook (attachment). Owner: ben_carter — delivery by Tue 2026-09-01.
2) Catalyst to share: (a) sample prompt sets, (b) representative input sizes and traffic profile. Owner: Sara — share by Mon 2026-08-31.
3) Technical scoping call with engineering (streaming + function calls deep dive). Owner: marissa_cole + karthik_iyer — schedule week of 2026-09-06.
4) Security/Compliance prep: high-level KMS/HSM and data retention Q&A during scoping call; follow with SOC2 evidence if needed. Owner: ben_carter — kick off after scoping call.

Attachments: redwood-inference-integration-playbook.pdf (summary + API examples), sample-prompt-sets.csv (your sample prompts you mentioned).

Questions for you before the scoping call:
- Is Azure the only cloud we must support for the pilot or is a hybrid (Redwood-hosted for non-sensitive traffic) acceptable?
- Are strict JSON schema failures considered fatal (block execution) or should Redwood surface them and let your ingest pipeline decide?

If that looks right, I’ll circulate a calendar invite for a technical scoping session and include Marissa (runtime/inference) and Karthik (architectural constraints).

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Sara Thompson <sara@catalyst.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 17:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration & inference goals — Catalyst AI

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick clarifications: we do need the pilot to run in our Azure VNET (no hybrid for pilot). We can provide the sample prompt sets by Monday, and we’ll include traffic histograms and a CSV of typical candidate counts per query.

On JSON schema failures: prefer that Redwood surface validation failures in metadata (non-fatal) for the pilot — our ingestion layer will decide how to handle them. For production we may move to stricter enforcement depending on QA.

Please put me down for the week of 9/6 for scoping; mornings PST are best. Looking forward to the playbook.

Best,
Sara
Head of Search & Relevance | Catalyst AI
sara@catalyst.ai

- Confirmed: pilot in Azure VNET only. We’ll validate our Private deployment checklist against your egress rules.
- For streaming + partial rerank, we typically implement a progressive rerank signal (first-pass lightweight embed score + async full model rerank) — we’ll sketch a proposal for expected P95 numbers vs. cost.

Proposed agenda for scoping call (30–45 mins):
1) Walkthrough of your current rerank pipeline and candidate generation (15 mins)
2) Redwood runtime: streaming, function calling, and structured output enforcement (10 mins)
3) Embedding batch throughput and format alignment (5–10 mins)
4) Security constraints & deployment checklist (5–10 mins)

I’ll drop a Doodle/Invite with morning PST slots for 9/6 and 9/8. In the meantime, here’s the drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-catalyst-integration

- Define a minimal SDK surface (JS + Go) that exposes: streaming responses, function-calling hooks, structured-output schema enforcement, and a switchable model alias for A/B.
- Preliminary checklist for Azure VNET deployment (KMS/HSM, private endpoints, egress exceptions) and expected lead time.
